After an unusual three-week gap between macOS developer beta 4 and beta 5, Apple has followed up last Monday's release with beta 6 just one week later. Here's what's new.

Apple releases macOS 27 developer beta 6

With the launch of the official version approaching, Apple is now pushing out the sixth beta of macOS 27 Golden Gate to all developers.

Last week's beta 5 gave apps like Siri, Chess, and Safari fresh new icons, but otherwise had no other notable new features (or bug fixes).

macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces a standalone Siri app, a unified rounded corner design across all system windows and apps, and AI-powered features for Shortcuts and Safari that let users create extensions and automation flows with simple commands.

The system also adds a new "pull-to-refresh" gesture to Safari, which many see as an early signal that Apple is pushing macOS to become more touch-friendly, paving the way for the rumored touchscreen MacBook Pro.

macOS 27 Golden Gate also significantly improves iPhone Mirroring, letting users resize windows into different aspect ratios—a change also seen as a prelude to the rumored foldable iPhone Ultra expected to debut next month.

macOS 27 Golden Gate official build number: 26A5416b.

How to install the macOS 27 Golden Gate beta

Here are the steps to install the fifth developer beta of macOS 27 Golden Gate:

  • Back up your Mac
  • Open System Settings
  • Go to General → Software Update
  • Click the "i" next to Beta Updates
  • From the drop-down menu in the top-right corner, select macOS Developer Golden Gate Beta
  • Click Done

Have you spotted any new features in this macOS 27 Golden Gate beta? Drop them in the comments.
